canonical_claim: The envelope drops `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version`; `CityHash64` is no longer part of envelope processing.
The envelope header is built before payload streaming, so header construction has no payload dependency and remains compatible with S3-native staging.
After codecs v3, `Formats/` contains per-object format files and includes only IO primitives and identifier vocabulary, never `CasBackend.h` or subsystem headers.

The CA in-commit upload-retry stack is caller-agnostic: INSERT and MERGE share `putBlob`, `uploadFromSource`, and `CasRequestController`, and both keep the staged scratch temporary alive across retries.

`CasRequestControl` uses a 16-attempt, 90-second default operation budget, while `putBlob` has an outer eight-round loop that catches only `ABORTED`; deterministic local failures are rethrown immediately.
The S36 dedup-on-TO-CA check uses deterministic `repeat('cas-move-dedup-probe-', 100)` payloads so a second move of byte-identical content must observe `CasBlobPutDedup > 0` and `CasBlobPut == 0`.
Review finding №3 is refuted because `HEAD` precedes `GET`; a mixed result can contain newer bytes with an older token, and conditional consumers fail closed on that stale-token combination.

The controlled CAS body-upload path classifies 5xx and 429 conditional-write results as `Unresolved`, resolves them by HEAD, and retries within `attempt_timeout_ms=5000`, `operation_deadline_ms=90000`, and `max_attempts=16` with capped-exponential backoff.

`CasJsonWriter` is intended to replace `WriteBuffer` in all CAS text-format encode paths while preserving byte-identical output; the read side, `JsonObjectReader`, `src/IO/WriteHelpers.h`, and every on-wire byte remain unchanged.
The CAS string writer must be the single escaping path for all strings and must not offer a trust-based raw-string shortcut; its semantics are fixed to `escape_forward_slashes = false`.
The `RecordStream` family, including `cas_run`, must remain streaming and bounded by one line (`line_cap` 4 KiB), never by record count.

The `cas_run` writer assembles each NDJSON line in one reused `CasJsonWriter`, performs one bulk `WriteBuffer::write` per line, then calls `clear()` so capacity is retained and memory stays bounded by the largest line.
Decoded interserver `ManifestEntry.path` values must be relative and contain no empty, `.` or `..` path segments; legal projection subdirectories remain valid.
`S3ObjectStorage` owns a lazily built single-attempt client clone and must rebuild it when the disk client rotates, while CAS conditional writes select `ObjectStorageRetryProfile::SingleAttempt`.
Non-S3 backends may ignore `ObjectStorageRetryProfile::SingleAttempt`; only CAS sets the profile today and an unsupported backend need not throw at profile-selection time.

The dedicated CAS upload pool is disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`, and its getter fails loudly when uninitialized or when the configured pool size is zero. Blob fan-out uses a dedicated server-wide pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; the caller only submits and joins, pool size 1 is valid and serializes work, the getter fails if uninitialized, and a configured size of 0 is rejected.; The multi-commit design uses one dedicated CAS upload pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; upload tasks return `DepEntry` values and merge them into `build->deps` only after joining.
In the phased engine, a per-part manifest edge is durably precommitted before any of that part's blobs are uploaded, and promote runs only after all of that part's blobs are complete.

`Cas::PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` must not read or mutate `PartWriteTxn` `build` state, because the transaction is single-writer; it returns a `BlobUploadResult` containing the complete dependency effect and outcome.; `PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` is a side-effect-free upload primitive that returns value-only results and does not mutate transaction state; upload results are merged into each part's build serially after the join.

Condemned-local resurrection uses a byte-weighted semaphore whose weight is the checked header-plus-payload size; a blob heavier than total capacity gets exclusive access after the semaphore drains, and the permit is released after `putOverwrite` and body destruction.

Blob fan-out groups pending blobs by `BlobRef`, rejects conflicting declared sizes, launches exactly one task per unique ref, and merges exactly one dependency result per unique ref.; Duplicate blob references collapse to one upload task, and conflicting duplicate declared sizes are rejected with `LOGICAL_ERROR`.

`BlobUploadRequest` is a public CAS-owned type containing `BlobRef`, a source descriptor, and `declared_size`; `BlobUploadResult` contains `BlobRef`, the complete `BlobDepRecord`, and one of seven upload outcomes.
Publish-confirm uses protocol version 11 with `content_addressed_confirm` as the confirm action parameter and `content_addressed_source_token` as the relink-offer response cookie.
The removed snapshot/ref-log field `pl` is explicitly rejected in both former wire locations, including negative decoding tests, rather than silently ignored.

`HoleyListBackend` omits one chosen durable key from one qualifying `list` call while leaving exact `get` and `head` for that key functional, modeling an incomplete enumeration without modeling a particular pagination mechanism.

A fail-closed read-only `Backend` decorator should make every `put*` and `delete*` operation throw `READONLY`; `ca-gc-rebuild`'s single `gc/state` CAS must be an explicit exception rather than an accidental hole.

The observed hole firing was not explained by a phantom key, concurrent ref-object deletion, stale-epoch minting, out-of-order appends, late landing, page-limit mismatch, or different key filters: the hole keys were `HEAD`-present, there were zero ref-object deletes in the relevant minute, all 65,263 uploads were ordered by writer epoch, and both walks used limit 1000 and `parseRefObjectKey`.

At firing time, `HEAD` distinguishes the two opposite enumeration defects: `present` means a durable object was omitted by an enumeration, while `absent` means the other enumeration returned a nonexistent key and indicts the client or iterator; this distinction cannot be recovered after legitimate deletion.

The HEAD-before-GET pair is a standing-veto protocol step; its cost is measured as the number of edges multiplied by approximately 0.9 ms per round trip, without proposing removal.; The HEAD-before-GET pair is a protocol step and must not be removed as a cheap performance optimization.; The HEAD-before-GET pair remains a protocol step under the standing veto; the proposed cache removes whole redundant edges and therefore does not remove the HEAD from an edge that is still fetched.
An `EpochSeal` transaction contains exactly one seal operation; `prev_epoch_seal` is required on sequence 1 of every non-genesis epoch, including an empty epoch, and is forbidden elsewhere.

Stage A's `EpochSeal` grammar requires exactly one `EpochSeal` operation, requires `prev_epoch_seal` at sequence 1 when `writer_epoch > life_epoch`, and forbids it at genesis `{life_epoch, 1}` and elsewhere.
